options.content:
JQL-approximate-count gauges scraped from the **jira-bridge** metrics endpoint (`:9093/metrics`) into VictoriaMetrics, per the Jira-metrics→Grafana epic (ka-0000004505). Primary series: `gardenio_jira_issues{query,project}` — the `query` label is the metric name (open_bugs, wip, …); `project` scopes the JQL (v1 = PE,DEVOPS).

Use the **Project** template variable (top-left) to slice every count and trend to a single project scope, or leave it on _All_ for the cross-project total.

_Counts are Jira `approximate-count` estimates — good for trends, may wobble run-to-run. Tile colors are **illustrative** heuristics (green = healthy, amber = watch, red = alarm) so the counts carry color semantics; tune the threshold steps to your team's SLA targets._

**Age / SLA (ka-0000000282):** `gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds` (snapshot histogram of per-issue age) + `gardenio_jira_issue_oldest_age_seconds` ground the **SLA age & burn-down** row — oldest-open age, age p50/p90/p95, and N-day SLA-breach counts (`_count − _bucket{le="Nd"}`).

panels.title: Open bugs
panels.description: issuetype = Bug AND statusCategory != Done. Thresholds are illustrative (amber ≥ 250, red ≥ 750) — tune to your bug-SLA.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_issues{query="open_bugs"} series for $project — the JQL-count exporter published nothing, so the count is UNKNOWN, not zero open bugs. Check “Scrape errors” in the Collector-health row at the bottom.

panels.title: Open high-sev bugs
panels.description: issuetype = Bug AND priority in (High,Highest) AND statusCategory != Done — SLA pressure. Thresholds are illustrative (amber ≥ 25, red ≥ 50) — high-sev bugs matter at small counts.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_issues{query="open_bugs_high"} series for $project — the exporter published nothing, so this is UNKNOWN, not zero. A live exporter with no matches renders 0. Check the Collector-health row.

panels.title: Open high-priority
panels.description: priority in (High,Highest) AND statusCategory != Done. Thresholds are illustrative (amber ≥ 500, red ≥ 1500) — tune to capacity.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_issues{query="open_high_priority"} series for $project — the exporter published nothing, so this is UNKNOWN, not zero. Check the Collector-health row at the bottom.

panels.title: Work in progress
panels.description: statusCategory = "In Progress". Thresholds are illustrative (amber ≥ 300, red ≥ 700) — high WIP signals flow overload; tune to team capacity.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_issues{query="wip"} series for $project — the exporter published nothing, so WIP is UNKNOWN, not zero. Check the Collector-health row at the bottom.

panels.title: Backlog
panels.description: statusCategory != Done — total open issues. Thresholds are illustrative (amber ≥ 3000, red ≥ 6000) — tune to your backlog target.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_issues{query="backlog"} series for $project — the exporter published nothing, so the backlog is UNKNOWN, not empty. Check the Collector-health row at the bottom.

panels.title: Reopened (7d)
panels.description: status CHANGED FROM Resolved AFTER -7d — rework rate. Thresholds are illustrative (amber ≥ 1, red ≥ 5) — any reopen is worth a look.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_issues{query="reopened_7d"} series for $project — the exporter published nothing, so this is UNKNOWN, not zero reopens. Check the Collector-health row at the bottom.

panels.title: Created vs resolved (rolling 7d)
panels.description: created_7d (backlog growth) vs resolved_7d (throughput). Resolved > created = backlog shrinking.

defaults.noValue: no created_7d / resolved_7d series for $project in this range — the exporter published neither side of the throughput pair, so flow is UNKNOWN. Empty is not a stalled team; check “Scrape errors” at the bottom of this board.

panels.title: Backlog trend (burn-down)
panels.description: Open issues (statusCategory != Done) sampled over time, faceted by the project label. A falling line = backlog burning down; a rising line = backlog growing. v1 runs a single combined PE,DEVOPS query, so today this is one series; it splits automatically as per-project queries are added.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_issues{query="backlog"} series for $project in this range — there is no trend to draw because the exporter published nothing, not because the backlog is flat at zero.

panels.title: Net backlog change trend (7d rolling)
panels.description: created_7d − resolved_7d sampled over time. Bars above zero (red) = backlog grew that week; at/below zero (green) = backlog held or shrank. The trajectory shows whether the team is pulling ahead of, or falling behind, incoming work — the trend framing of the single-value stat below. Empty-branch liveness: every `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="jira-bridge"} == 1`, so a 0 appears only while the jira-bridge exporter is actually being scraped — a dark bridge leaves the panel empty instead of painting a reassuring zero.

defaults.noValue: no created_7d / resolved_7d series for $project in this range — the difference is UNDEFINED, not a net-zero backlog change. Check the Collector-health row at the bottom.

targets.expr: (max(gardenio_jira_issues{query="created_7d", project=~"$project"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1))) - (max(gardenio_jira_issues{query="resolved_7d", project=~"$project"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1)))

panels.title: Net backlog change (7d)
panels.description: created_7d − resolved_7d. Positive = backlog grew this week; negative = backlog shrank (resolved outpaced created). Empty-branch liveness: every `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="jira-bridge"} == 1`, so a 0 appears only while the jira-bridge exporter is actually being scraped — a dark bridge leaves the panel empty instead of painting a reassuring zero.

defaults.noValue: no value — the exporter published neither created_7d nor resolved_7d for $project (or the datasource did not answer). Not “net zero”: a live exporter renders a number. Check the Collector-health row.

targets.expr: (max(gardenio_jira_issues{query="created_7d", project=~"$project"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1))) - (max(gardenio_jira_issues{query="resolved_7d", project=~"$project"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1)))

panels.title: Resolved ÷ created (7d)
panels.description: resolved_7d / created_7d. ≥ 1 = keeping up or draining backlog (green); < 1 = falling behind (red). Guarded against divide-by-zero when no issues were created. Empty-branch liveness: every `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="jira-bridge"} == 1`, so a 0 appears only while the jira-bridge exporter is actually being scraped — a dark bridge leaves the panel empty instead of painting a reassuring zero.

defaults.noValue: no value — the exporter published neither created_7d nor resolved_7d for $project (or the datasource did not answer). The ratio is UNDEFINED, not 0. Check the Collector-health row.

targets.expr: (max(gardenio_jira_issues{query="resolved_7d", project=~"$project"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1))) / clamp_min((max(gardenio_jira_issues{query="created_7d", project=~"$project"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1))), 1)

panels.title: Oldest open bug
panels.description: gardenio_jira_issue_oldest_age_seconds{query="open_bugs_age"} — age of the single oldest open bug. Grounded from the per-issue age export (not derivable from count gauges). Thresholds illustrative (amber ≥ 90d, red ≥ 180d).

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_issue_oldest_age_seconds series for $project — the age exporter published nothing, so oldest-age is UNKNOWN, not “no old bugs”. Check the Collector-health row at the bottom.

panels.title: Open bug age p95
panels.description: 95th-percentile age of open bugs via histogram_quantile over gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds buckets. Thresholds illustrative (amber ≥ 30d, red ≥ 90d).

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds_bucket samples for $project — histogram_quantile has no buckets to read, so p95 is UNDEFINED, not young. Check the Collector-health row at the bottom.

panels.title: Bugs older than 30d
panels.description: Open bugs breaching a 30-day SLA: _count − _bucket{le=30d}. A grounded SLA-breach count from the per-issue age histogram. Thresholds illustrative (amber ≥ 50, red ≥ 200). Empty-branch liveness: every `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="jira-bridge"} == 1`, so a 0 appears only while the jira-bridge exporter is actually being scraped — a dark bridge leaves the panel empty instead of painting a reassuring zero.

defaults.noValue: no value — the age histogram published no _count/_bucket series for $project, so the >30d band is UNKNOWN, not zero. A live exporter with no aged bugs renders 0.

targets.expr: (sum(gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds_count{query="open_bugs_age", project=~"$project"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1))) - (sum(gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds_bucket{query="open_bugs_age", project=~"$project", le="2.592e+06"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1)))

panels.title: Bugs older than 90d
panels.description: Open bugs breaching a 90-day SLA: _count − _bucket{le=90d}. Thresholds illustrative (amber ≥ 25, red ≥ 100) — an aged-out long tail. Empty-branch liveness: every `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="jira-bridge"} == 1`, so a 0 appears only while the jira-bridge exporter is actually being scraped — a dark bridge leaves the panel empty instead of painting a reassuring zero.

defaults.noValue: no value — the age histogram published no _count/_bucket series for $project, so the >90d band is UNKNOWN, not zero. A live exporter with no aged bugs renders 0.

targets.expr: (sum(gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds_count{query="open_bugs_age", project=~"$project"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1))) - (sum(gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds_bucket{query="open_bugs_age", project=~"$project", le="7.776e+06"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1)))

panels.title: Open bug age percentiles (p50/p90/p95)
panels.description: Age percentiles of open bugs over time via histogram_quantile on the per-issue age snapshot histogram. A falling band = the open-bug population is getting younger (SLA-age burning down); a rising band = bugs are aging. This is the true age burn-down the count-only gauges could not ground.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds_bucket samples for $project in this range — the percentile fan is UNDEFINED, not flat. Check the Collector-health row at the bottom.

panels.title: Open bugs by SLA-age band (burn-down)
panels.description: Count of open bugs older than 7d / 30d / 90d over time, each derived as _count − _bucket{le=Nd} on the per-issue age histogram. Watch each band trend toward zero as aged bugs are resolved — the grounded SLA-age burn-down. Empty-branch liveness: every `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="jira-bridge"} == 1`, so a 0 appears only while the jira-bridge exporter is actually being scraped — a dark bridge leaves the panel empty instead of painting a reassuring zero.

defaults.noValue: no age-histogram series for $project in this range — none of the three SLA bands can be computed, which is UNKNOWN rather than an empty backlog. Check the Collector-health row at the bottom.

targets.expr: (sum(gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds_count{query="open_bugs_age", project=~"$project"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1))) - (sum(gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds_bucket{query="open_bugs_age", project=~"$project", le="604800"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1)))

(sum(gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds_count{query="open_bugs_age", project=~"$project"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1))) - (sum(gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds_bucket{query="open_bugs_age", project=~"$project", le="2.592e+06"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1)))

(sum(gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds_count{query="open_bugs_age", project=~"$project"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1))) - (sum(gardenio_jira_issue_age_seconds_bucket{query="open_bugs_age", project=~"$project", le="7.776e+06"}) or (vector(0) and (max(up{component="jira-bridge"}) == 1)))

panels.title: Scrape errors (rate)
panels.description:
Per-query Jira API scrape-error rate. Sustained > 0 = the exporter cannot reach Jira or the JQL is failing.

gardenio_jira_scrape_errors_total is a label-gated CounterVec: a {query} series only exists after that query has failed at least once since the current controller process started, so an absent series is NOT proof the error path is observable. The flat 0 here is EARNED, not fabricated — it is baselined off `sum by (query) (gardenio_jira_scrape_duration_seconds) * 0`, the per-query gauge the scrape loop rewrites every cycle. So a 0 means "the scraper ran this query and did not fail"; if the exporter itself stops, that anchor disappears too and the panel falls through to its noValue instead of painting a confident 0 (ka-0000006531, replaces `or vector(0)`).

defaults.noValue: jira exporter not reporting — no gardenio_jira_scrape_duration_seconds samples in window, so the scrape-error rate is UNKNOWN (not 0)

panels.title: Scrape duration
panels.description: Per-query Jira approximate-count call latency. Rising duration warns of Jira rate-limit backoff (Retry-After).

defaults.noValue: gardenio_jira_scrape_duration_seconds returned nothing. This is the board's liveness anchor and it cannot certify itself: either the exporter has completed no JQL scrape since the jira-bridge booted, or the bridge is not being scraped at all. Treat every issue count above this panel as unverified and resolve with up{component="jira-bridge"} on Gardenio — System Health.

title: Jira — Metrics
description: Jira project health from the jira-bridge JQL-count exporter: open bug and priority counts, created-vs-resolved flow, backlog trend, bug-age percentiles and SLA-age bands, plus exporter scrape health. Open this for 'is the backlog growing, and is the oldest bug ageing past policy?'.
